_comment: Catalog exclusions, applied before resolving. `scripts` drops uploads whose ORIGINAL YouTube title contains that writing system — the reliable signal for language, since the public IMDb datasets carry no language or country field. `groups` drops whole config/channels.json groups. `imdbIds` and `ytIds` are precise manual escape hatches. Everything here is reported in the run summary, so nothing disappears silently.
_groups_MartialArts: Only channel is the Wu Tang Collection: 2,372 features resolving at 13.4%, and its 888 unresolved uploads are per-distributor English release names that IMDb carries under no aka. Dropped by the owner's decision on 2026-09-06, not by a heuristic.
_groups_Polish: Only channel is @alefilmy, dropped 2026-09-07 on a licensing judgement, not a match-quality one — its matches are correct, which is the problem. 14 of its 15 accepted films are from 2000 or later (Memento, Michael Clayton, Paddington, Need for Speed, Sinister 2, Arlington Road), spanning Newmarket, Warner, StudioCanal, DreamWorks, Focus and Screen Gems — a spread no single licensor holds — and every upload carries Polish lektor voiceover. The channel has no `currentReleases` marker, and channels.json reserves that for the four rights holders; by its own stated test a modern match on an unmarked channel is anomalous. The score floor was the only thing holding the other 89 back: they sit in low-score at a uniform 44+12+17+10=79, so any loosening of §4 aimed at the yearless-neutral shape would have published them. Note `fct_upload.licensed` reads 1 on all of them and means nothing here — it is YouTube's contentDetails.licensedContent, which says a Content ID owner claimed the video, not that the uploader holds rights.
_ytIds_CineMo: CineMo, 2026-09-07. A licensing call like the alefilmy one, but the channel is MIXED, so the group hammer would have destroyed a real catalogue: its Filipino films (A Mother's Story, Home Alone da Riber, Action Is Not Missing) are its own and stay. The 14 below are Western studio and direct-to-video action titles uploaded under a separate convention — '<Star> in <TITLE> | Action | Full Movie HD in English' rather than the channel's own '<Title> | FULL MOVIE | <cast> | CineMo'. None were ever served: checked against the live catalog.json, 0 of 14 are in it, but all 14 are accept in the warehouse and would have shipped on the next build-catalog dispatch. ytIds, not imdbIds, and that distinction is load-bearing: tt3779300 (War Pigs) is ALSO on The Midnight Screening, which is a currentReleases rights holder and accepts it legitimately. A global imdbIds exclusion would have removed that licensed copy too. ytIds is channel-specific by construction and cannot collaterally drop another channel's copy, now or later. The title pattern that found these is a search tool, not a verdict — it has false positives. It flagged tt7415582 'Riding in Tandem', a genuine Filipino CineMo film caught only because its own title contains ' in ', and it flagged two probable WRONG matches on generic one-word titles: tt0050762 'Nine Lives' (1957) on an upload whose listed cast belongs to a different film, and tt5162870 'Underworld' (2008). Those three are deliberately NOT excluded; the last two are resolver bugs to investigate, not licensing. Extended the same day to the review tier as well, 14 accepted plus 14 in review, 28 total. Review entries are never served, so they were not exposure today — but several sit at confidence 88-92, above the 85 floor and held only by the recent-year flag or a short margin, and the whole point of the conf-82 work in item 5 is to promote things out of exactly this queue. Leaving them would have meant a later +3 publishing them by the back door. Only the '<Star> in <TITLE>' marker was used to select these, never the '| Action |' one: the second marker is what produced the false positives named above. Final five added 2026-09-07, taking the list to 33. These are the last of the channel's foreign uploads and were found by splitting the confidence-82 band on the channel's OWN convention (a `| CineMo` suffix or `| FULL MOVIE |`) rather than on the unreliable `| Action |` marker: 47 of the 52 are its genuine Filipino catalogue (Mga mata sa dilim, Asuang, Ilawod, AWOL, Corpus Delicti, My Candidate, Padre de Familia, Resbak, #Y, Sta. Nina) and only 5 are foreign -- Daughter of the Wolf, The Expendables 3, Cabin Fever 3, Gallowwalkers, Ninja. An earlier note put this residue at 52, which was the unreliable marker's error, not a real count. The cross-channel check earned its keep a second and third time here: tt7615052 (Daughter of the Wolf) and tt1182921 (Ninja) are ALSO on Movie Central, a currentReleases rights holder, exactly as tt3779300 was on The Midnight Screening. A global imdbIds exclusion would have deleted three licensed copies. Run the join before every exclusion.
